title: Workload migration comparison: on-premises to cloud

slides.purpose: Bring one workload to two possible destinations.
slides.notes: W1 is an illustrative workload, not a measured customer system. Both destinations remain open.

scene.staticDescription: W1 sits between on-premises and cloud, connected to both. Demand, requirements and total cost guide the decision.

cues.semantic: The admin presents W1, then considers both destinations

slides.purpose: Inspect existing capacity without claiming waste from CPU use.

scene.staticDescription: W1 connects to the rack and a fixed-capacity chart with changing illustrative demand. Patching, power and recovery remain adjacent. CPU alone does not establish waste or savings.

cues.semantic: Rack inspection reveals installed capacity, demand and operational work

slides.notes: No measured utilisation percentage, savings estimate or claim of waste. The chart has illustrative relative units.

slides.purpose: Make incoming work cause capacity changes and qualify cost.
slides.takeaway: Capacity follows demand. Savings need proof.

scene.staticDescription: W1 sends a batch into a capacity pool. Two units expand to five, then return to two as the batch drains. Migration, ongoing usage and egress must enter the comparison.

cues.semantic: Visible batches cause expansion and contraction, not independent oscillating bars

slides.notes: Illustrative sequence, not a promise of instantaneous autoscaling. Policies, service limits and minimum capacity require validation.

slides.purpose: Each connected station leaves a visible evidence artifact.

scene.staticDescription: W1 traverses four connected stations. Outputs are a demand baseline, dependency map with a latency question, like-for-like cost ranges and a reversible test with pass criteria. No station invents a successful outcome.

cues.semantic: Admin follows W1 and each station produces a tangible comparison artifact

slides.notes: The cost ranges are deliberately unpriced. Latency and recovery are test questions, not verified claims.

slides.purpose: Keep both conditional routes and the next action on screen.
slides.takeaway: Move what fits. Retain what does not.
slides.notes: Final composition holds for at least three seconds, with W1, admin, evidence criteria and both conditional routes. No celebration or exit.

scene.staticDescription: W1 remains at a decision gate: requirements, total cost and pilot evidence lead to conditional move or retain routes. Pilot one workload is the persistent next action.

cues.semantic: Admin considers the evidence and presents both routes; W1 never disappears

blocks.label: Let evidence lead, not platform preference.

slides.notes: Review-only representative layout; omitted from the timed story.

blocks.label: A reversible test
blocks.body: Time-box the pilot and keep rollback.

blocks.label: A conditional decision
blocks.body: Requirements, costs and pilot evidence must support the route.

slides.notes: Review-only third representative layout; omitted from the timed story.
